article.name: GraQle
article.summary: GraQle is a Python knowledge-graph and agent reasoning framework. Its durable project graph and separate in-process reasoning-round memory have distinct storage and scope models. This review is based on pinned public source and documentation; no runtime or benchmark result is claimed.

who_what.text: The official README identifies Quantamix Solutions as the builder and presents GraQle as a persistent knowledge graph and reasoning framework for agents.
The reviewed product has CLI, Python, MCP, and server surfaces; local project graph persistence and in-process reasoning-round memory are separate components.

architecture.text: Graqle stores typed CogniNode records and CogniEdge relations in a NetworkX graph, with graph JSON as the primary persistence tier and optional Neo4j and Neptune projections.
The learn commands create knowledge, entity, node, and file records with domain, tag, source, path, or timestamp properties and can add inferred semantic or keyword connections.
ReasoningMemory is a separate in-process store keyed by agent, round, and node, with tenant-bound entry dictionaries and a bounded per-tenant snapshot history.

behavior.text: Learning commands add or replace graph nodes and add edges; the inspected CLI read/modify/write path uses a file lock, while serialization validates graph structure and writes the node-link JSON representation under a cross-platform lock.

The inspected core graph operations expose node and edge additions but no first-class delete/forget operation was located in those operations or the learn commands. Erasure from replicas or backups was not established.

Reasoning activates a selected subgraph through a configured ranking and backend, then sends it to an orchestrator. The path supports direct filename lookup, semantic activation memory boosts, and other activator strategies.

Round memory stores result values with agent, round, node, confidence, clearance, and TRACE metadata; it counts differing agent findings on the same node as contradictions and applies configurable confidence decay.

Memory summaries decay and confidence-filter entries, rank by confidence, redact values above viewer clearance, and cap output at 8,000 characters. Snapshots and rollback are scoped to the bound tenant slice.

metrics.evidence: Graph activation and reasoning paths were inspected; no benchmark answers were generated or scored.
Confidence decay, contradiction tracking, and graph update behavior were inspected; no correction probes were run.
No first-class graph delete path was located in the inspected operations; no post-delete probes were run.
Tenant validation and binding plus documented project separation were inspected; no cross-tenant or cross-project workload was executed.
Provenance fields and citation instructions were inspected; no returned claim was adjudicated against source text.
No runtime timing samples were collected.
The code includes result/graph metrics and the README reports a fixture-specific RSS comparison; no GraQle token, cost, or persistent-storage measurements were collected in this review.

limits.text: The persistent project graph and in-memory reasoning-round store have distinct persistence, lifecycle, and scope behavior; neither component's properties should be generalized to every product surface.

Tenant IDs are normalized and instances bind to one tenant, but validation does not assert tenant existence and the code delegates authorization to callers. Non-default scope is gated by an environment variable.
Clearance redaction replaces the protected value while retaining source-agent identity, confidence, and TRACE metadata; metadata exposure may matter to a deployment's threat model.
The inspected graph operations and learn commands did not expose a first-class delete path. Deletion, replica cleanup, and backup erasure remain unknown.
Source and provenance fields and citation prompts do not establish factual correctness or evidence entailment. The upstream RSS comparison is tied to its documented fixture and was not reproduced.

benchmark.note: No GraQle runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was run. Source observations, upstream-reported RSS figures, and project evaluation definitions are not GraQle benchmark results.
